In another shell, a\\\\\\\\nminimal smoke check is:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n```sh\\\\\\\\ncurl --fail http://127.0.0.1:3000/health\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe response is `{\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"ok\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\":true}`.  Before submitting a change, at minimum run\\\\\\\\n`ruby -c app.rb`; run the cumulative benchmark evaluator when it is available\\\\\\\\nin the surrounding benchmark environment.  Do not start a long-running server\\\\\\\\nas part of static verification.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Entry points and layout\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThis intentionally minimal Rails API is kept in a small number of root files:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- `run.sh` is the server command used by the benchmark.\\\\\\\\n- `config.ru` requires `app.rb` and exposes `Rails.application` to Rack.\\\\\\\\n- `app.rb` defines the Rails application, controllers, shared domain helpers,\\\\\\\\n  SQLite storage, and all routes.  It loads only the Rails controller stack;\\\\\\\\n  Active Record and Rails migrations are deliberately not used.\\\\\\\\n- `Gemfile` and `Gemfile.lock` pin the Rails/Rack/Puma runtime.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Request routing and state\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n`DndApi.routes` at the end of `app.rb` is the authoritative route list.\\\\\\\\nControllers inherit from `ApplicationController`, which parses request JSON,\\\\\\\\nnormalizes integer inputs, and renders the common invalid-request response.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n`GameStorage` owns the SQLite connection, schema setup, reset operation, and a\\\\\\\\nprocess-local mutex.  Its database file is `game.db` beside `app.rb` and\\\\\\\\npersists users, combat sessions, compendium records, and campaign records\\\\\\\\nacross server restarts.  `GameStorage.initialize_schema!` runs during boot.\\\\\\\\nAll storage reads and writes are made inside `GameStorage.synchronize` so the\\\\\\\\nsingle shared SQLite connection is used safely by Puma threads.  Storage reset\\\\\\\\nis intentionally exposed through `POST /v1/storage/reset` and is the only API\\\\\\\\noperation that clears persisted state.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## API/domain groupings\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Core rules: health, dice statistics, ability checks, initiative ordering,\\\\\\\\n  characters, and adjusted encounter XP.\\\\\\\\n- Combat and auth: persistent combat sessions/conditions/turn advancement and\\\\\\\\n  SQLite-backed user registration/login.  `CombatSessionState` and\\\\\\\\n  `AuthCredentials` hold their non-routing mechanics.\\\\\\\\n- Compendium and campaigns: monster/item records, campaign characters/events,\\\\\\\\n  persistent scheduled sessions/attendance, and a campaign state view.\\\\\\\\n- PHB utilities: spell slots, long-rest recovery, and equipment load.\\\\\\\\n- DM tools: encounter building from campaign/compendium data, deterministic\\\\\\\\n  tier-one loot, and the latest campaign-event recap.  `EncounterMath` is\\\\\\\\n  shared by the core and DM encounter endpoints to keep their XP behavior in\\\\\\\\n  lockstep.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Safe extension and testing conventions\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nPreserve the existing route, status-code, response-shape, validation, and\\\\\\\\npersistence contracts: the benchmark is cumulative.  Put controller-only\\\\\\\\nrequest handling in the relevant controller and extract only genuinely shared,\\\\\\\\nside-effect-free logic into a focused module.  Keep database access inside the\\\\\\\\nstorage mutex and use parameterized SQL.  Add schema changes to\\\\\\\\n`GameStorage.initialize_schema!` and ensure `reset!` drops any new tables.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nPrefer deterministic ordering and values; existing APIs intentionally sort\\\\\\\\ninitiative and query campaign collections by insertion order.  Exercise a\\\\\\\\nfeature through HTTP after resetting storage, then rerun the cumulative suite\\\\\\\\nto catch interactions with earlier domains.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n--- RUN ---\\\\\\\\n#!/usr/bin/env Each entry is a method-qualified\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  `http.ServeMux` pattern and maps directly to its handler.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- The handlers are grouped by domain: core dice/check/character helpers;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  combat sessions; authentication; storage administration; compendium monsters\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  and items; campaign state; PHB rules; and DM tools.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- The storage helpers (`initializeStorage`, schema functions, `runSQLite`, and\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  `querySQLite`) own the file-backed persistence boundary.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- The small helpers at the bottom handle strict JSON decoding and JSON error/\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  success responses.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n`run.sh` is the supported launcher and deliberately runs `go run .` in the\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nforeground. `go.mod` pins the module to Go 1.26 with no third-party Go\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ndependencies.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## State and persistence\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n`game.db` is created in the current working directory. The storage adapter\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ninvokes `/usr/bin/sqlite3` and stores users, combat sessions, compendium\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nrecords, campaigns, campaign characters, and campaign events. JSON blobs are\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nused for structured records; users and combat sessions are also loaded into\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nthe process-local maps during startup. The storage status and reset endpoints\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexpose the existing schema lifecycle.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThree mutex-protected state areas exist: user state, combat state, and storage\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nstate. Where reset needs all three, it locks user state, then combat state,\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nthen storage state. Code that touches multiple areas must preserve this order\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nto avoid deadlocks. Persistence helpers called while user or combat state is\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nheld acquire only the storage mutex.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Safe extension conventions\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nPreserve the existing API contract exactly: method, route pattern, status code,\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nJSON shape, validation message, and persistence behavior are observable.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nRegister any accepted new route in `newRouter`; keep method-qualified patterns\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ninstead of adding ad-hoc method checks. Decode request bodies through\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n`decodeJSON`, which enforces a 1 MiB limit, rejects unknown fields, and rejects\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ntrailing JSON values. Send responses through `respondJSON` or `badRequest` to\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nretain the JSON content type and error format.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nKeep validation deterministic, use the existing storage helpers for durable\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nrecords, and test both successful and invalid requests.
